import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Stable field conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace StableFieldConjecture

/-- A structure has a stable complete theory if no formula has the order property. Here the order
property is expressed by the existence of finite half-graphs of every size. -/
def IsStable (L : FirstOrder.Language) (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (n m : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)),
      ∀ N : ℕ, ∃ (a : Fin N → Fin n → M) (b : Fin N → Fin m → M),
        ∀ i j, φ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

/--
The stable field conjecture: every infinite field whose complete first-order theory in the
language of rings is stable is separably closed.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 12]
theorem stable_field_conjecture :
    ∀ (K : Type*) [Field K] [Infinite K],
      @IsStable FirstOrder.Language.ring K
        (FirstOrder.Ring.compatibleRingOfRing K).toStructure → IsSepClosed K := by
  sorry

end StableFieldConjecture
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “stable first-order theory” as stability of the complete theory Th(K) in the pure language of rings, as specified by the decomposition and the background article.

Defined stability by absence of the order property. The order property is expressed as one fixed formula realizing finite half-graphs of every natural-number size in K. For the complete theory Th(K), this is equivalent by compactness to an infinite half-graph in some model, and unlike requiring infinite sequences in K itself it does not assume that K is saturated.

Represented the two finite tuples of variables of a formula by `Fin n ⊕ Fin m`, and the two families of tuples by functions `Fin N → Fin n → M` and `Fin N → Fin m → M`. Used `i ≤ j`, matching the half-graph convention in the background article.
Used `FirstOrder.Ring.compatibleRingOfRing K` to give each field its canonical structure in Mathlib’s language of rings, and used Mathlib’s `Infinite K` and `IsSepClosed K` directly.

import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Algebra.Ring.Basic
import Mathlib.ModelTheory.Satisfiability

/-!
# Stable field conjecture

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, *Stable theory*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
-/

namespace StableFieldConjecture

open FirstOrder

/--
A first-order theory is stable if it has no order property: no formula defines an infinite
half-graph on two sequences of finite tuples in a model of the theory.
-/
def IsStable (T : Language.ring.Theory) : Prop :=
  ¬ ∃ (m n : ℕ) (φ : Language.ring.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n))
      (M : Language.Theory.ModelType.{0, 0, 0} T) (a : ℕ → Fin m → M) (b : ℕ → Fin n → M),
    ∀ i j, φ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

/--
The stable field conjecture: every infinite field whose complete first-order theory in the
language of rings is stable is separably closed.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 03 12]
theorem stable_field_conjecture (K : Type*) [Field K] [Infinite K] :
    let _ := Ring.compatibleRingOfRing K
    IsStable (Language.ring.completeTheory K) → IsSepClosed K := by
  sorry

end StableFieldConjecture
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “stable” using the equivalent no-order-property characterization stated in the supplied Wikipedia article: there is no ring-language formula and pair of sequences of finite tuples in a model of the theory realizing the infinite half-graph pattern φ(aᵢ,bⱼ) ↔ i ≤ j.
Applied stability to Mathlib's `Language.ring.completeTheory K`, with the canonical compatible ring-language structure supplied by `FirstOrder.Ring.compatibleRingOfRing K`.

Quantified order-property witnesses in a universe-0 bundled model. This is faithful for the countable language of rings: if an order-property witness exists, downward Löwenheim–Skolem yields such a witness in a small model.
Represented “every infinite field” by an arbitrary type `K` with `[Field K] [Infinite K]`, and represented “separably closed” by Mathlib's `IsSepClosed K`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Stable field conjecture

The stable field conjecture states that every infinite field with a stable first-order theory
is separably closed. Here the first-order theory of a field $K$ is its complete theory in the
language of rings, and a complete theory $T$ is *stable* if no formula has the order property
in $T$, i.e. there are no formula $\varphi(\bar{x}, \bar{y})$ and sequences of tuples
$(\bar{a}_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$, $(\bar{b}_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ in a model of $T$ such
that $\varphi(\bar{a}_i, \bar{b}_j)$ holds if and only if $i \le j$.

The finite fields are excluded because every finite structure has a stable theory but a finite
field is not separably closed.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
-/

namespace StableFieldConjecture

open FirstOrder Language

universe u v

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}}

/-- A formula `φ(x̄, ȳ)`, with variables split as `Fin m ⊕ Fin n`, has the *order property* in
the theory `T` if there are a model `M` of `T` and sequences `(aᵢ)ᵢ`, `(bⱼ)ⱼ` of tuples
in `M` indexed by `ℕ` such that `φ(aᵢ, bⱼ)` holds in `M` if and only if `i ≤ j`. -/
def HasOrderProperty (T : L.Theory) {m n : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (a : ℕ → Fin m → M) (b : ℕ → Fin n → M),
    ∀ i j, φ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- A theory `T` is *stable* if no formula has the order property in `T`. -/
def IsStable (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ {m n : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin n)), ¬ HasOrderProperty T φ

/-- The theory of dense linear orders without endpoints is not stable: the formula `x ≤ y` has
the order property, witnessed in `ℚ`. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_isStable_dlo : ¬ IsStable Language.order.dlo := by
  letI := orderStructure ℚ
  intro h
  refine h (leSymb.formula₂ (var (Sum.inl 0)) (var (Sum.inr 0)) :
    Language.order.Formula (Fin 1 ⊕ Fin 1)) ?_
  refine ⟨Theory.ModelType.of _ ℚ, fun i _ => (i : ℚ), fun j _ => (j : ℚ), fun i j => ?_⟩
  simp

/--
**Stable field conjecture.** Every infinite field whose complete first-order theory in the
language of rings is stable is separably closed.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 12]
theorem stable_field_conjecture (K : Type*) [Field K] [Infinite K] [Ring.CompatibleRing K]
    (hK : IsStable (Language.ring.completeTheory K)) : IsSepClosed K := by
  sorry

end StableFieldConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the statement; the notes correctly identify that stability must be introduced and that the converse and superstable case are out of scope.
modeling_decisions: Stability is formalized via the order-property characterization (Wikipedia: 'A common alternate definition of stable theories is that they do not have the order property'), not via counting types (κ-stable for some infinite κ); these are classically equivalent, and the order property is far simpler to state with Mathlib's existing `Formula.Realize` API.

The order property is stated at the level of the theory `Th(K)` ('some model of T'), not inside `K` itself; this matches the source ('field with a stable first-order theory') and avoids the known discrepancy where a structure can lack infinite half-graphs while its theory still has the order property.

The witness model in `HasOrderProperty` is taken in universe `max u v` (so `Type 0` for the ring language), following Mathlib's `Theory.IsSatisfiable` convention; by downward Löwenheim–Skolem this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe.

The first-order theory of `K` is `Language.ring.completeTheory K` under the hypothesis `[Ring.CompatibleRing K]`, Mathlib's recommended pattern; since the ring language has exactly the five function symbols and no relations, `CompatibleRing` forces the structure to be the field's own operations, so this is Th(K) in the language of rings.
Tuples of variables are encoded as `Fin m ⊕ Fin n` with `Sum.elim`, sequences are indexed by `ℕ`, and the half-graph condition is `i ≤ j`, exactly as in the Wikipedia text.

`Infinite K` is required as in the statement (finite fields are stable but not separably closed); `IsSepClosed` is Mathlib's class. Only the forward implication is stated; Wood's converse and the superstable (Macintyre, Cherlin–Shelah) case are not included, per the decomposition notes.

The bespoke definitions are kept in the problem file (the harness reads a single file); a proved `category test` declaration `not_isStable_dlo` (DLO is unstable, witnessed in ℚ) is included as the basic API test required by CONTRIBUTING.md for bespoke definitions.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Stable field conjecture

The stable field conjecture states that every infinite field whose first-order theory, in the
language of rings, is stable is separably closed.

A complete first-order theory $T$ is *stable* if no formula has the order property in a model
of $T$. A formula $\phi(\bar x, \bar y)$ has the *order property* in a structure $M$ if there
are sequences of tuples $(\bar a_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $(\bar b_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ in
$M$ such that $M \models \phi(\bar a_i, \bar b_j)$ if and only if $i \le j$. This is equivalent
to $T$ being $\kappa$-stable for some infinite cardinal $\kappa$, that is, to $T$ having at most
$\kappa$ complete types over every parameter set of size $\kappa$.

The restriction to infinite fields is necessary: a finite field has a stable theory but is not
separably closed. The converse of the conjecture is a theorem of Wood: every separably closed
field has a stable theory. The superstable case is known (Macintyre, Cherlin–Shelah): an infinite
superstable field is algebraically closed.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia: Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
- [Wikipedia: Separably closed field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Separably_closed_field)
-/

namespace StableFieldConjecture

open FirstOrder Language Ring

universe u v

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}}

/-- A formula $\phi(\bar x, \bar y)$ has the *order property* in the `L`-structure `M` if there
are sequences $(\bar a_i)_{i \in \mathbb{N}}$ and $(\bar b_j)_{j \in \mathbb{N}}$ of tuples in `M`
such that $M \models \phi(\bar a_i, \bar b_j)$ holds if and only if $i \le j$. -/
def HasOrderProperty {α β : Type*} (M : Type*) [L.Structure M] (φ : L.Formula (α ⊕ β)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (a : ℕ → α → M) (b : ℕ → β → M), ∀ i j, φ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- A first-order theory `T` is *stable* if no formula $\phi(\bar x, \bar y)$ has the order
property in any model of `T`. For a complete theory this is equivalent to `T` being
$\kappa$-stable for some infinite cardinal $\kappa$.

The models are taken in `Type (max u v)`, as in `FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelsBoundedFormula`;
by compactness this does not change the notion. -/
def IsStable (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (n m : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)),
    ¬ HasOrderProperty M φ

/-- **Stable field conjecture.** Every infinite field $K$ whose complete first-order theory
$\mathrm{Th}(K)$, in the language of rings, is stable is separably closed.

The field `K` is regarded as a structure for the language of rings through `CompatibleRing K`,
which forces the interpretation of the ring symbols to agree with the field operations of `K`.
Every field admits such a structure (`FirstOrder.Ring.compatibleRingOfRing`), and it is unique. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 12]
theorem stable_field_conjecture (K : Type*) [Field K] [CompatibleRing K] [Infinite K]
    (hK : IsStable (Language.ring.completeTheory K)) : IsSepClosed K := by
  sorry

end StableFieldConjecture

modeling_decisions: 'Stable first-order theory' of a field K is read as: the complete theory Th(K) of K as a structure in Mathlib's `Language.ring` (symbols +, *, -, 0, 1) is stable. K is made a ring-language structure via `[FirstOrder.Ring.CompatibleRing K]`, Mathlib's recommended idiom; I checked that every field admits such an instance (`compatibleRingOfRing`) and that the instance is unique, so the hypothesis is neither vacuous nor about a different structure.

Stability is defined via the order property (Wikipedia's 'common alternate definition'): T is stable iff for every model M of T, all n m : ℕ and every formula φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m), there are no sequences a b : ℕ → tuples in M with M ⊨ φ(a i, b j) ↔ i ≤ j. The `i ≤ j` convention is Wikipedia's (other texts use i < j; equivalent). The κ-stability (type-counting) definition was not used because it is equivalent for complete theories and would require substantially more bespoke infrastructure (types over parameter sets, cardinal counting) with more room for error.

In `IsStable`, models are quantified in `Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T` (so in `Type 0` for the ring language), mirroring Mathlib's `Theory.ModelsBoundedFormula`. By compactness this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe (an infinite half-graph in some model gives arbitrarily long finite ones in every model, and compactness then yields a model in `Type (max u v)` with an infinite one).
Formulas are parameter-free with variables split as `Fin n ⊕ Fin m`; the order property with parameters is equivalent (parameters can be absorbed into the ȳ tuple).
The 'infinite' hypothesis is `[Infinite K]`; the module docstring explains that finite fields are stable but not separably closed.

The two definitions are generic and could arguably live in `FormalConjecturesForMathlib/ModelTheory/`; per the task constraints they are kept in the problem file (as e.g. `VaughtConjecture.lean` does with `numberOfCountableModels`).

The converse (Wood) and the superstable case (Macintyre, Cherlin–Shelah) are only mentioned in the module docstring for context; they are not stated as declarations, as the decomposition table requires.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Stable field conjecture

The stable field conjecture states that every infinite field with a stable first-order
theory is separably closed.

*References:*
* [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
* [Wikipedia, Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
-/

namespace StableFieldConjecture

open FirstOrder Language Ring

variable {L : Language} (M : Type*) [L.Structure M]

/-- A partitioned formula `φ(x̄; ȳ)` of `L` *has the order property* in the `L`-structure `M`
if for every `n` there are tuples `a₀, …, aₙ₋₁` and `b₀, …, bₙ₋₁` in `M` such that
`M ⊨ φ(aᵢ; bⱼ)` holds if and only if `i ≤ j`.

By compactness, this holds if and only if `φ` has the order property in the complete theory
`Th(M)` of `M`, i.e. if and only if there are a model `N` of `Th(M)` and infinite sequences
`(aᵢ)ᵢ∈ℕ`, `(bⱼ)ⱼ∈ℕ` of tuples in `N` such that `N ⊨ φ(aᵢ; bⱼ) ↔ i ≤ j`. The existence of such
infinite sequences in `M` itself implies this condition, but not conversely, so the finite
version is used. -/
def HasOrderProperty {m k : ℕ} (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin k)) : Prop :=
  ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (a : Fin n → Fin m → M) (b : Fin n → Fin k → M),
    ∀ i j, φ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

variable (L)

/-- An `L`-structure `M` is *stable* if its complete first-order theory `Th(M)` is stable, i.e.
no formula `φ(x̄; ȳ)` has the order property in `M`. This is equivalent to `Th(M)` being
`κ`-stable for some infinite cardinal `κ`, i.e. to the set of complete types over any subset of
cardinality `κ` of any model of `Th(M)` having cardinality `κ`. -/
def IsStable : Prop :=
  ∀ (m k : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin m ⊕ Fin k)), ¬ HasOrderProperty M φ

/-- Every finite structure is stable. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem isStable_of_finite [Finite M] : IsStable L M := by
  intro m k φ hφ
  obtain ⟨a, b, hab⟩ := hφ (Nat.card (Fin m → M) + 1)
  have ha : Function.Injective a := by
    intro i j hij
    by_contra hne
    rcases lt_or_gt_of_ne hne with h | h
    · have h1 := (hab i i).mpr le_rfl
      rw [hij] at h1
      exact absurd ((hab j i).mp h1) (not_le.mpr h)
    · have h1 := (hab j j).mpr le_rfl
      rw [← hij] at h1
      exact absurd ((hab i j).mp h1) (not_le.mpr h)
  have := Nat.card_le_card_of_injective a ha
  simp at this

/-- The natural numbers with their order are not stable: the formula `x ≤ y` has the order
property. -/
@[category test, AMS 3]
theorem not_isStable_nat_order :
    letI := orderStructure ℕ
    ¬ IsStable Language.order ℕ := by
  letI := orderStructure ℕ
  intro h
  refine h 1 1 ((Term.var (Sum.inl (Sum.inl 0))).le (Term.var (Sum.inl (Sum.inr 0)))) fun n => ?_
  refine ⟨fun i _ => i, fun j _ => j, fun i j => ?_⟩
  simp [Formula.Realize]

/-- **Stable field conjecture.** Every infinite field `K` whose complete first-order theory
`Th(K)`, in the language of rings `{+, ·, -, 0, 1}`, is stable is separably closed.

The hypothesis `CompatibleRing K` equips `K` with its `Language.ring`-structure in which the
symbols are interpreted by the field operations; every field admits such a structure
(`compatibleRingOfRing`) and it is unique. Stability does not change when the definable
operation `⁻¹` is added to the language. The field `K` must be infinite: finite fields are
stable but not separably closed. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 12]
theorem stable_field_conjecture (K : Type*) [Field K] [Infinite K] [CompatibleRing K]
    (hK : IsStable Language.ring K) : IsSepClosed K := by
  sorry

end StableFieldConjecture

Stability of Th(K) is formalized on the structure K via the finitary order property (arbitrarily long finite half-graphs in K for a fixed partitioned formula). import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Stable field conjecture

The stable field conjecture states that every infinite field with a stable first-order theory
is separably closed.

Mathlib does not define stability of a first-order theory, so it is defined here.
A theory `T` is stable if no formula has the order property in `T`. A formula `φ(x̄, ȳ)` has
the order property in `T` if there are a model `M` of `T` and sequences `(aᵢ)`, `(bⱼ)` of tuples
in `M`, indexed by `ℕ`, such that `M ⊨ φ(aᵢ, bⱼ)` if and only if `i ≤ j`. For a complete theory
this is equivalent to `T` being `κ`-stable for some infinite cardinal `κ`.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Wikipedia, Stable theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stable_theory)
-/

namespace StableFieldConjecture

open FirstOrder Language

universe u v

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}}

/-- A formula `φ(x̄, ȳ)` of `L`, whose free variables are split as `α ⊕ β`, has the
order property in the theory `T` if there are a model `M` of `T` and sequences `(aᵢ)`, `(bⱼ)`
of tuples in `M`, indexed by `ℕ`, such that `M ⊨ φ(aᵢ, bⱼ)` if and only if `i ≤ j`. -/
def HasOrderProperty (T : L.Theory) {α β : Type*} (φ : L.Formula (α ⊕ β)) : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T) (a : ℕ → α → M) (b : ℕ → β → M),
    ∀ i j, φ.Realize (Sum.elim (a i) (b j)) ↔ i ≤ j

/-- A theory `T` is stable if no formula `φ(x̄, ȳ)` has the order property in `T`. -/
def IsStable (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n m : ℕ) (φ : L.Formula (Fin n ⊕ Fin m)), ¬ HasOrderProperty T φ

/-- The **stable field conjecture**: every infinite field `K` whose complete first-order theory
in the language of rings is stable is separably closed. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3 12]
theorem stable_field_conjecture (K : Type*) [Field K] [FirstOrder.Ring.CompatibleRing K]
    [Infinite K] (hK : IsStable (Language.ring.completeTheory K)) : IsSepClosed K := by
  sorry

end StableFieldConjecture
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition matches the statement.
modeling_decisions: Stability is defined via the order property (no formula defines an infinite half graph on ℕ-indexed sequences of tuples in some model of T, with the `i ≤ j` convention of the Wikipedia article), rather than via κ-stability (type counting). For complete theories such as Th(K) these are classically equivalent (Shelah); the article gives both and calls the order-property version a common alternate definition.

The theory is the complete theory of K in Mathlib's `Language.ring` (+, *, -, 0, 1); the compatibility of this first-order structure with the field operations is expressed by the Mathlib-recommended instance hypothesis `[FirstOrder.Ring.CompatibleRing K]`, which every field satisfies via `compatibleRingOfRing`. The language of fields with an inverse symbol would give an interdefinable structure, so stability is unaffected.

In `HasOrderProperty`, the witnessing model ranges over `Theory.ModelType.{u, v, max u v} T` (models in universe `max u v`, which is `Type` for the ring language), the same convention Mathlib uses for `Theory.IsSatisfiable`. By downward Löwenheim–Skolem/compactness this is equivalent to allowing models in any universe; note also that K itself may live in a higher universe than the models quantified over, which is harmless for the same reason.

The order property is checked in some model of Th(K) rather than in K itself: the ℕ-indexed (infinite) order property in the specific structure K is not in general equivalent to stability of Th(K), so the theory-level definition is the faithful one.
`[Infinite K]` is kept as a hypothesis exactly as in the statement; it is necessary since finite fields are stable but not separably closed.

Formulas are taken with variables `Fin n ⊕ Fin m` for all n m : ℕ, i.e. arbitrary finite tuples x̄, ȳ. Only the conjecture itself is stated; the known converse (Wood) and the solved superstable case are not part of the statement, in line with the decomposition notes.
